title: HEAD_DIM 64 + WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 0.3
description: Two constants at depth 10: HEAD_DIM 128->64 (10 heads of 64, n_embd unchanged at 640) and WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5->0.3; nothing else.
reflection: val_bpb 1.000945 vs 0.988076 baseline: +0.0129, ~27 sigma on the pooled 4.8e-4 floor. A clear NEGATIVE, and the negative is the warmdown, not the head count. My run carries HEAD_DIM 64, which the four pure-HD64 arms this round measure independently; subtracting their number isolates the schedule term, and it is large and positive. Shortening the cooldown from half the budget to 30% costs roughly +0.017. I was wrong about the direction: I argued from WSD-schedule literature that 50% sits past the optimum and that 30% would buy ~10% more effective LR for free. It does raise average lrm from 0.75 to 0.825, and that made training worse, not better, at this horizon. Two things that make this worth the slot anyway. (1) The LR-schedule axis is LIVE and STEEP - 0.2 of warmdown ratio is worth 0.017 bpb, which is larger than every architectural effect the cell has found except model size. Nothing else we have touched has that gradient. (2) The gradient has a sign: less decay is much worse, so the profitable probe is MORE decay - WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.7, or 1.0 which is pure linear decay from step 0. That is now the single best-motivated unrun experiment on the table and it is one constant. Secondary measurement, previously assumed: HEAD_DIM 64 is NOT quite free in throughput. 1091 steps / 286.0M tokens / MFU 40.91% against the baseline's 1119 / 293.3M / 41.94% - 10 heads of 64 run ~2.5% slower than 5 of 128 despite identical params, FLOPs and VRAM (34.7GB, unchanged). Six of us wrote 'exactly zero cost' in our proposals; it is zero in FLOPs, not in wall-clock, and at a fixed time budget that is a real ~7M-token tax.
